description: A small reactive UI language and compiler: .sui source becomes a self-contained web app or a desktop executable. Documentation is organized for humans and coding agents.

invariants.rule: Run `simpleui check --json` after editing a .sui file and fix all errors before building or previewing.
Interpolated text and attributes are escaped automatically. Raw HTML interpolation is intentionally unavailable; never try to inject markup from data.
Treat API, file, CSV, URL and iframe input as untrusted. Check returned errors and show them; rejected iframe URLs must produce the built-in visible error.
A dynamic `style:` value must be wrapped in `cssSafe(expr)`. Static developer-authored styles are trusted.
Dynamic classes are filtered to the app class allow-list. Prefer static classes for layout.
Dynamic HTTP/WebSocket URLs require `*Safe` with a literal allow-list. Do not concatenate untrusted data into a literal URL to bypass this.
Iframes default to `sandbox=""` and `no-referrer`. Dynamic `src` requires a literal `srcAllow` allow-list; rejected data is not loaded and shows an error.
Table cells are inert (`textContent`). Use `table.display`, check its error, and preserve the table's style. Use `;formula=escape` for CSV opened by spreadsheets.
Desktop file and command access is granted only at build time with `--allow-dir` / `--allow-exec`. Validate user-supplied names on top of the bridge checks.
Use the manifest/recipes instead of inventing syntax. Search `simpleui docs --search <term>` and read the canonical doc before coding.
Canonical documentation, code comments and UI strings are English. If an Italian `_IT` counterpart exists, update it in the same change.

recipes.title: Drag and drop
recipes.when: The interface must reorder rows or accept files and directories dropped from the operating system.
steps: Give each source and target a stable `dragKey` / `dropKey`; use `onDrop` to update the array with `moveItem`.
Bind a string state with `dropFiles: state` and display it with `value: state` on an input or textarea.
Use `pickFiles: state` on a file control or button when the native dialog is preferable to dragging; configure it with `accept`, `multiple`, `directory`.
Use `drag.files()` for immediate metadata and `drag.error()` for rejected input.
Open `docs/GUI_EDITOR.md` for inspector steps and for the list/table/component editing limits.
Treat dropped names as untrusted text; browsers expose names/relative paths, not absolute paths.

recipes.title: File type analyzer with a Go backend
recipes.when: The app must upload selected/dropped files to a Go service, analyze them in the backend and render the results in a table.
steps: Select files with `pickFiles` or `dropFiles`; keep a visible state field.
Call `http.postFiles("/api/analyze")` inside an async function and show a loading state.
Validate the JSON response and pass `{columns, rows}` to `table.display`.
Enforce upload size/count limits and treat filenames as untrusted text in the backend.

recipes.title: Local form + reactive table
recipes.when: A local-only app needs forms, derived state, validation and tabular data.
steps: Declare states for form fields, status and rows.
Bind inputs with `value:` / `checked:` and wire actions with `onClick:`.
Use `table name:` for the model and `table.display` for data.
Show loading, empty and error states explicitly.

recipes.title: Remote JSON API + table
recipes.when: A remote service returns JSON that should become a read-only or editable table.
steps: Import `http` and `json` from std.
Use a literal URL for a fixed endpoint; otherwise use `getSafe` with a literal allow-list.
Check both HTTP and JSON errors and render them.
Pass the parsed data to `table.display` and check its error.

recipes.title: Remote CRUD form
recipes.when: The interface must send user input to a remote service and update a local view.
steps: Validate fields before sending.
Use `http.postSafe` for dynamic destinations and a literal allow-list.
Serialize with `json.stringify`; never build JSON by string concatenation.
On success, refresh the local rows or table; on error, show the returned error.

recipes.title: Polling dashboard
recipes.when: A dashboard must refresh metrics periodically without a WebSocket.
steps: Use `onLoad:` to start `interval(ms, refresh)`.
Keep status separate from data.
Guard against overlapping refreshes if the request is slow.
Render a stable empty/loading/error state.

recipes.title: Desktop files and commands
recipes.when: The app must read/write local files or run a helper executable.
steps: Build with explicit `--allow-dir` / `--allow-exec` capabilities.
Validate user-supplied names before calling fs/exec.
Use `dialog.pickFile`/`pickDirectory` for user-driven native paths; they still require fs/exec capabilities.
Show bridge errors; do not retry blindly.
Never assume web builds have these capabilities.

recipes.title: Spreadsheet ingestion
recipes.when: The user provides XLSX or ODS files that should populate a table.
steps: Convert XLSX/ODS upstream with `sheet2json` or the local converter service.
Receive JSON/CSV, validate the response and show conversion errors.
Use `table.display` for rendering and `table.exportText` for export.
Do not parse binary spreadsheets in the browser.

recipes.title: Embed external content safely
recipes.when: The interface must show a video, map, document or other third-party page.
steps: Use a literal `src` for a trusted endpoint; otherwise add a literal `srcAllow` origin/path allow-list.
Start with the default empty sandbox; add only the tokens actually needed.
Keep `referrerpolicy` at `no-referrer` unless there is a reason.
Never use `srcdoc`; malformed iframe data is rejected with a visible message.

recipes.title: Security review
recipes.when: The app consumes untrusted text, URLs, files, tables, iframes or desktop capabilities.
steps: Check every untrusted value is data, never markup/CSS/URL syntax.
Use `cssSafe`, `*Safe` URLs, `srcAllow`, and table `textContent`.
Show errors from parsers, HTTP, table and bridge calls.
Run the security examples and the full test suite.
